To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Mössbauer effect in superconducting tin was found to be reduced by 1.3±0.2 parts per thousand at the superconducting transition temperature, and that the Möss-bauer effect was found to be independent of magnetic field up to 6 Tesla at 4.2 K, which is consistent with a superconducting gap of 3.6 meV.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Debye-Wall factor of the tin lattice is increased in the superconductivity state, but the change is small.
the Mössbauer-effect is not influenced by the superconducting phase transition of tin.
the Mößbauer effect in the superconductors Sn and In is not affected in any way by the transition into the superconducting phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the superconductivity of tin is not accompanied by a change of the lattice dynamics.
the Debye-Wall factor of the tin metal source is increased by 0,4±0,1% in the superconductivity.
the superconducting transition is accompanied by a change in the lattice dynamics of the order of magnitude of 10−3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Debye-Wall factor is not the same above and below the superconducting transition.
the Debye temperature of tin in the superconductivestate is higher by about 0.4% compared to the normal state.
the Mössbauer effect can be used to measure the superconducting transition in a metal.
